title: Pazyryk kurgans and the Issyk Golden Man
summary: Burial mounds in the Pazyryk valley of the Altai held the world's oldest known pile carpet, found in Barrow 5 (excavated by S. I. Rudenko in 1949) and dated by the Hermitage to the 5th–4th century BC. In Kazakhstan, a mound at Issyk near Almaty, excavated by Kemal Akishev in 1969, yielded the "Golden Man" with more than 4,000 gold pieces.

uncertainty.note: Span is the Hermitage date for the Pazyryk carpet (5th–4th century BC). Voices on Central Asia dates the Pazyryk culture to the 6th–2nd centuries BC; the Astana Times gives the Saka at circa fourth–third century BCE with grave goods of the fifth–fourth century BCE.
